facts.text: Swaledale sprang to life when the Mason City and Fort Dodge Railroad built a line through the area, creating a station and platting the town on May 5.
Agriculture has always driven Swaledale’s economy, with early grocery stores, blacksmith shops, and a grain elevator that still operates today as the Five‑Star Co‑op.
Swaledale celebrated its 100th year in 1992 with a veterans memorial in City Park and a community cookbook titled 100 Years of History and Favorite Recipes.
The Swaledale Museum serves as a port of entry for historical material, offering collections, research, and exhibits that chronicle the town’s past.
Before European settlers, the Swaledale area was part of a tallgrass prairie that hosted Sioux and Winnebago tribes, whose hunting grounds overlapped in northern Iowa.
